  "title": "Step-Level Faithfulness-Gated Rejection Decoding: Enforcing CoT Faithfulness via Hidden-State Consistency Probes",
  "core_problem": "LLM reasoning traces are frequently unfaithful to internal computations (15-20% of correct CoT outputs are unfaithful per FaithCoT-Bench ICLR 2026; 25-39% acknowledgment rates per Anthropic 2025; up to 60% failure to update after causal intervention per ICLR 2026 work). The Illusion of Reasoning (arXiv 2603.22816) further demonstrates that faithfulness varies dramatically by domain and training objective—DeepSeek-R1 shows 91-93% step necessity on math vs. 4% for non-reasoning DeepSeek-V3.2—revealing that unfaithfulness is systematic, not random. While probe-guided decoding has been shown to improve CORRECTNESS at step level (DHC, AAAI 2026), and Token-Guard (ICLR 2026) performs token-level factual hallucination control via latent-space scoring with regeneration, no existing method targets FAITHFULNESS specifically during generation. Correctness probes miss the 15-20% of outputs that are correct-but-unfaithful. Token-Guard addresses factuality (text vs. world knowledge), not faithfulness (text vs. internal computation). Training-time approaches (FaithRL, REMUL) improve faithfulness on average but cannot guarantee step-level faithfulness at inference time for any specific input. Meanwhile, Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay (arXiv 2602.11201) documents a 'Mapping Gap'—models encode correct internal representations while failing to use them in decoding—and a 'Reasoning Horizon' at 70-85% of chain length beyond which reasoning tokens have negligible causal effect. These findings constrain where and how inference-time faithfulness interventions can succeed.",
  "opportunity": "Four convergent findings create a precise opening: (1) Step-level probe-guided decoding WORKS for correctness (DHC, AAAI 2026 demonstrates beam search guided by attention-head probes significantly outperforms baselines); (2) Trace-level probe-guided interventions FAIL (Hidden Error Awareness, May 2026, shows best-of-N ≈ random, self-correction hurts by -3%); (3) Faithfulness is orthogonal to correctness (FaithCoT-Bench documents 15-20% correct-but-unfaithful instances); (4) Probes CAN detect internal-external divergence—Reasoning Theater (Goodfire, arXiv 2603.05488) shows probes detect performative CoT at 87.98% accuracy with performativity rate 0.417 on MMLU, and the 'Single Direction of Truth' (arXiv 2507.23221) isolates a linear direction in residual stream separating faithful from hallucinated text. The Mapping Gap from Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay (arXiv 2602.11201) initially appears threatening—models encode correct representations but fail to decode them—but actually SUPPORTS detection: the systematic divergence between internal state and output creates a learnable signal. A probe need not bridge the gap; it need only detect WHEN the gap is large. The reconciliation across all findings is clear: step-level selection succeeds because probes have high per-step discrimination (0.95 AUROC) but poor cross-trace ranking; faithfulness is an unaddressed dimension; and probes can detect the internal-external divergence that constitutes unfaithfulness. This creates the opportunity for step-level faithfulness-gated rejection decoding with hidden-state diversity verification.",
  "landscape": "**Probe-guided decoding for correctness**: Deep Hidden Cognition (DHC, AAAI 2026, arXiv 2507.10007) trains linear probes on attention head activations to predict step correctness, then uses step-level beam search to select among M candidates. Targets correctness only; does not measure or improve faithfulness. **ReProbe** (arXiv 2511.06209) develops transformer-based probes (<10M params) on frozen LLM internal states matching or exceeding PRMs 810x larger for step-level verification—demonstrates the informativeness of internal states for reasoning quality assessment. **Failed interventions**: Hidden Error Awareness (arXiv 2605.09502, May 2026) shows 0.95 AUROC probes predict CoT correctness but four interventions fail—probe-guided best-of-N ≈ random (trace-level selection), self-correction hurts -3% (reuses same computation), activation steering is fragile, patching destroys coherence. Key insight: signal is diagnostic at trace level but selection works at step level (as DHC shows). **Token-level hallucination control**: Token-Guard (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2601.21969) performs token-level hallucination detection via latent-space cosine similarity + probability hybrid scoring, with segment-level hallucination risk scores and iterative pruning/regeneration. Targets factual hallucination (text vs. world knowledge) at token granularity—fundamentally different from reasoning faithfulness (text vs. internal computation) at step granularity. SFGRD differs in three ways: (a) targets faithfulness rather than factuality, requiring probes that compare text semantics against internal computation, not just token-level consistency; (b) operates at step level rather than token level, matching the granularity at which reasoning faithfulness is defined and measured; (c) uses trained probes rather than unsupervised cosine similarity, because faithfulness is not reducible to local coherence. **Step-level hidden-state evaluation**: STEP (arXiv 2601.09093) trains lightweight step scorers on hidden states for trace quality estimation with GPU memory-aware pruning, reducing latency 45-70% while improving accuracy—targets efficiency via trace pruning, not faithfulness enforcement. **Streaming detection**: Streaming Hallucination Detection (arXiv 2601.02170) frames hallucination as evolving latent state with prefix-level tracking—detection only, no correction mechanism. **Monitoring Decoding** (ACL 2025 Findings, arXiv 2503.03106) does token-level factuality monitoring with tree-based regeneration for QA/general text—targets factuality of claims against world knowledge, not faithfulness of reasoning to internal computation. **Hidden-state geometry**: Where Does Reasoning Break (arXiv 2605.13772, May 2026) uses transport geometry on hidden states for step-level hallucination detection—detection only, no intervention. ICR Probe (ACL 2025) tracks cross-layer hidden state dynamics for hallucination detection. **Internal-external divergence detection**: Reasoning Theater (Goodfire, arXiv 2603.05488) shows probes detect performative CoT at 87.98% accuracy on MMLU—models 'know' their answer early but continue generating decorative reasoning. Performativity rate of 0.417 on easy tasks vs. 0.012 on hard tasks (GPQA-Diamond), demonstrating that internal-external divergence is probe-detectable. A Single Direction of Truth (arXiv 2507.23221) isolates a single linear direction in residual stream separating hallucinated from faithful text, achieving 5-27 point improvements over baselines—demonstrates that faithfulness/hallucination leaves a linear signature in residual stream activations. **Mechanistic faithfulness analysis**: Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay (arXiv 2602.11201) introduces NLDD for step-level faithfulness measurement using corruption-based confidence drops. Documents the 'Mapping Gap' (models encode correct representations at 82% probe accuracy but achieve 0% task performance) and 'Reasoning Horizon' (steps beyond 70-85% of chain length have negligible causal effect). The Mapping Gap constrains probe-based approaches: probes can detect what information IS encoded, but the model may not USE it. However, for faithfulness detection (not correction), this is sufficient—detecting WHEN the gap is large IS detecting unfaithfulness. **Faithfulness variation**: The Illusion of Reasoning (arXiv 2603.22816) evaluates 13 frontier models across six domains, identifying three modes: 'genuine reasoning' (steps causally matter), 'scaffolding' (CoT helps but steps are interchangeable), and 'decoration' (CoT adds nothing). R1 models show 91-93% step necessity on math vs. 4% for non-reasoning V3.2—proving training objective determines faithfulness and motivating domain-aware evaluation. **Probe-based early exit**: Reasoning Models Know When They're Right (arXiv 2504.05419) uses probes for early exit during reasoning, saving 24% tokens. **Training-time faithfulness**: FaithRL (arXiv 2602.03507) optimizes step-level faithfulness via RL, reducing hallucination by 4.7 points. REMUL (arXiv 2602.16154) uses multi-listener RL for faithfulness. Stop Rewarding Hallucinated Steps (arXiv 2602.05897) uses faithfulness signals in RL. Counterfactual Simulation Training (arXiv 2602.20710) improves faithfulness via fine-tuning. All are training-time methods that improve average faithfulness but cannot enforce per-instance guarantees at inference. **Faithfulness measurement**: FUR (EMNLP 2025 Outstanding Paper) measures parametric faithfulness via unlearning—post-hoc. FaithCoT-Bench (ICLR 2026) benchmarks with 1000+ expert-annotated trajectories. Lie to Me (arXiv 2603.22582) documents faithfulness rates across 12 models. **Gap**: No method performs step-level rejection decoding gated by FAITHFULNESS probes (as distinct from correctness or factuality probes) during CoT generation, with verified computational diversity in regenerated alternatives.",
  "approach": "**Method: Step-Level Faithfulness-Gated Rejection Decoding (SFGRD)**

The approach proceeds in two phases: a feasibility pilot (Phase 1) that validates the core assumption, followed by the full SFGRD method (Phase 2).

**Phase 1: Feasibility Pilot (De-risking the Core Assumption)**

The central untested assumption is whether linear probes on residual stream activations can distinguish faithful from unfaithful reasoning steps. While probes detect correctness at 0.95 AUROC (Hidden Error Awareness) and performative reasoning at 87.98% accuracy (Reasoning Theater), no work has directly tested faithfulness detection at step level. Pilot design: (1) Take FaithCoT-Bench's ~300 unfaithful instances with step-level evidence (~1500 step-level labels across 4 domains). (2) Run Qwen3.6-27B on these problems, caching residual stream activations at every step boundary. (3) Train linear probe: f(h_residual) = σ(W^T h + b) per layer, with layer selection via validation AUROC. (4) Hold out 20% of expert annotations for evaluation. (5) Report AUROC on held-out set. **Go/no-go**: ≥0.80 AUROC → proceed to Phase 2; <0.80 → report as negative finding with analysis of what faithfulness dimensions are/aren't probe-detectable. **Cost**: <10 H100-hours. **Supporting evidence for feasibility**: (a) Reasoning Theater achieves 87.98% probe accuracy detecting performative CoT (internal-external divergence), (b) Single Direction of Truth isolates a linear faithfulness direction in residual stream, (c) Hidden Error Awareness shows 0.95 AUROC for error detection from hidden states. The task is conceptually between correctness detection (well-established) and full faithfulness measurement (untested)—detecting WHEN internal computation diverges from text, not WHY.

**Phase 2: SFGRD Method**

**Probe Architecture**: Train lightweight linear probes on RESIDUAL STREAM activations (not attention heads as in DHC) to predict whether a generated reasoning step faithfully reflects the model's internal computation. Residual stream encodes the full computational state—critical for faithfulness detection, which requires detecting divergence between text semantics and actual computation. Probe: f(h_residual) = σ(W^T h + b), trained per-layer with layer selection via validation AUROC. The choice of residual stream over attention heads is motivated by (a) the Single Direction of Truth finding that faithfulness signals are linearly encoded in residual stream, and (b) the Mapping Gap finding that residual stream encodes information not expressed in output—precisely the divergence we want to detect.

**Engaging with the Mapping Gap**: Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay (arXiv 2602.11201) shows models encode correct internal representations while failing to use them in decoding. This initially appears to threaten our approach: if probes detect what is ENCODED (not what is USED), they may not detect faithfulness. However, we argue the Mapping Gap SUPPORTS faithfulness detection: (a) The Mapping Gap IS the signal—when internal representations systematically diverge from output text, the residual stream at the final token of a step encodes both what the model computed and what it is about to output. A probe can learn to detect this divergence. (b) We do not need to BRIDGE the gap (make the model output what it internally knows); we need to DETECT it (flag when the output diverges from internal computation). (c) The Reasoning Theater finding that probes detect performative reasoning at 87.98% accuracy is empirical evidence that internal-external divergence IS probe-detectable. (d) If the pilot (Phase 1) confirms ≥0.80 AUROC, the question is resolved empirically.

**Training Data Pipeline**: (1) Primary ground truth: FaithCoT-Bench's ~300 unfaithful instances with step-level evidence across 4 domains, providing ~1500 step-level faithful/unfaithful labels from expert annotations. (2) Secondary expansion: Apply FUR unlearning protocol for ~3000 additional synthetic labels, with explicit acknowledgment that FUR measures 'parametric faithfulness' (does unlearning the step's fact change the answer?) while probes target 'representational faithfulness' (does text diverge from internal computation?). These overlap but are not identical—we train on both label types and report correlation as diagnostic. (3) Validation: Hold out 20% of FaithCoT-Bench expert annotations for probe evaluation.

**Step Boundary Detection**: For reasoning models (Qwen3.6-27B, DeepSeek-R1), step boundaries are identified via double-newline delimiters within <think> blocks. Minimum step length threshold of 20 tokens to avoid fragmentary segments. **Reasoning Horizon optimization**: Informed by the finding that steps beyond 70-85% of chain length have negligible causal effect (arXiv 2602.11201), we optionally concentrate monitoring on early/middle steps where faithfulness violations are most consequential. Ablation: full-chain monitoring vs. horizon-aware monitoring.

**Inference-Time Rejection Decoding with Hidden-State Diversity Verification**: After generating each reasoning step: (1) Extract residual stream activations at final token of step. (2) Faithfulness probe evaluates: p_faithful = f(h_residual). (3) If p_faithful > τ (threshold tuned on validation set): accept step, continue. (4) If p_faithful ≤ τ: REJECT step and regenerate with diversity constraints. (5) Maximum 3 rejection attempts per step; if all fail, accept highest-scoring attempt (graceful degradation).

**Multi-Mechanism Diversity for Regeneration** (addressing the 'same computation' problem): Hidden Error Awareness documents that 'the model generates its correction using the same flawed computation that produced the original error.' This implies the problem is computational, not articulatory—blocking surface n-grams may produce different text expressing the same unfaithful computation. We address this with a three-level diversity mechanism:

(a) **Surface diversity** (Level 1): 4-gram suppression of rejected step's text + temperature scaling (T=1.2→1.5 on successive rejections). This forces different token sequences as a baseline mechanism.

(b) **Computational diversity verification** (Level 2, novel): After regeneration, compare residual stream activations of regenerated step h_regen with rejected step h_orig. Compute cosine similarity: sim(h_regen, h_orig). If sim > δ (e.g., 0.95), the regeneration produced the same computation in different words—reject and escalate to Level 3. This directly tests whether surface diversity translates to computational diversity, turning the reviewer's concern into a measurable signal.

(c) **Conditioning perturbation** (Level 3, fallback): If Level 2 detects same-computation regeneration, perturb the conditioning: rephrase the previous accepted step using a lightweight paraphrase operation, then regenerate the current step from the modified prefix. This changes the input to the computation, not just the sampling.

**Key Differentiators from DHC**: (a) Targets faithfulness, not correctness—probes trained on faithfulness labels. (b) Uses rejection sampling with multi-level diversity rather than beam search—more efficient and specifically addresses the 'same computation' problem. (c) Residual stream probes (full computational state) vs. attention head probes (local reasoning patterns). (d) Hidden-state diversity verification ensures regeneration produces genuinely different computations.

**Key Differentiators from Token-Guard**: (a) Targets reasoning faithfulness (text vs. internal computation) vs. factual hallucination (text vs. world knowledge). (b) Operates at step level (matching faithfulness granularity) vs. token level. (c) Uses trained probes with faithfulness labels vs. unsupervised cosine similarity in latent space. (d) Includes computational diversity verification vs. simple local regeneration.

**Key Differentiators from Hidden Error Awareness's failed interventions**: (a) Step-level rejection (proven viable by DHC's success) vs. trace-level best-of-N (proven to fail). (b) Multi-level diversity mechanism with hidden-state verification prevents 'same flawed computation' problem. (c) Hard acceptance gate vs. soft ranking.

**Baselines**: (1) Greedy decoding (no intervention). (2) DHC beam search with correctness probes (reproduction). (3) DHC beam search with faithfulness probes (direct comparison—same probe, different decoding). (4) Self-consistency (majority voting). (5) Probe-guided best-of-N (replicating Hidden Error Awareness's failure as sanity check). (6) Token-Guard-style latent-space scoring adapted to step level (ablation to isolate contribution of trained faithfulness probes vs. unsupervised similarity).

**Evaluation**: Primary model: Qwen3.6-27B. Datasets: GSM8K (mathematical, where hidden-state findings are validated) + GPQA (knowledge-intensive, testing generalization—critical given Illusion of Reasoning's finding of dramatic domain variation). Metrics: (a) Faithfulness improvement via FaithCoT-Bench evaluation protocol (counterfactual intervention + unlearning test). (b) Accuracy preservation (≤1% degradation acceptable). (c) Latency overhead (target: <2x greedy). (d) Rejection rate and regeneration statistics. (e) Hidden-state similarity between original and regenerated steps (quantifying computational diversity). Extended evaluation (for camera-ready or follow-up): DeepSeek-R1-32B replication.

**Ablations**: (1) Residual stream vs. attention head probes. (2) Rejection sampling vs. beam search with faithfulness probes. (3) Diversity mechanism ablation: surface-only (n-gram blocking) vs. hidden-state diversity verification vs. conditioning perturbation vs. combined (tests the 'same computation' hypothesis directly). (4) Threshold sensitivity analysis. (5) Expert annotations vs. FUR synthetic labels for probe training (tests label source impact). (6) Full-chain monitoring vs. Reasoning Horizon-aware monitoring (tests efficiency optimization). (7) Probe layer selection.

**Explicit Failure Criteria**: (1) Probe AUROC < 0.80 on held-out FaithCoT-Bench data → faithfulness is not detectable from residual stream at step level (report as negative finding). (2) Faithfulness improvement < 2% over greedy decoding → step-level rejection doesn't help. (3) Accuracy degradation > 3% → faithfulness enforcement destroys correctness. (4) Hidden-state similarity between original and regenerated steps > 0.95 in > 50% of cases despite diversity mechanisms → forced diversity doesn't create alternative computation paths (report as evidence supporting Hidden Error Awareness's 'same computation' thesis). (5) SFGRD performs ≤ DHC with faithfulness probes → rejection sampling offers no advantage over beam search for faithfulness.",

(2) Faithfulness probe evaluates: p_faithful = f(h_residual). (3) If p_faithful > τ (threshold tuned on validation set): accept step, continue. (4) If p_faithful ≤ τ: REJECT step and regenerate with diversity constraints. (5) Maximum 3 rejection attempts per step; if all fail, accept highest-scoring attempt (graceful degradation).

This implies the problem is computational, not articulatory—blocking surface n-grams may produce different text expressing the same unfaithful computation. We address this with a three-level diversity mechanism:

(a) **Surface diversity** (Level 1): 4-gram suppression of rejected step's text + temperature scaling (T=1.2→1.5 on successive rejections). This forces different token sequences as a baseline mechanism.

(b) **Computational diversity verification** (Level 2, novel): After regeneration, compare residual stream activations of regenerated step h_regen with rejected step h_orig. (d) Hidden-state diversity verification ensures regeneration produces genuinely different computations.

(b) Operates at step level (matching faithfulness granularity) vs. token level. (c) Uses trained probes with faithfulness labels vs. unsupervised cosine similarity in latent space. (b) Multi-level diversity mechanism with hidden-state verification prevents 'same flawed computation' problem. (c) Hard acceptance gate vs. soft ranking.

(6) Full-chain monitoring vs. Reasoning Horizon-aware monitoring (tests efficiency optimization). (7) Probe layer selection.

# Paper Summary: Decoding Answers Before Chain-of-Thought

## Full Abstract
"As chain-of-thought (CoT) has become central to scaling reasoning capabilities in large language models (LLMs), it has also emerged as a promising tool for interpretability, suggesting the opportunity to understand model decisions through verbalized reasoning. However, the utility of CoT toward interpretability depends upon its faithfulness -- whether the model's stated reasoning reflects the underlying decision process. We provide mechanistic evidence that instruction-tuned models often determine their answer before generating CoT. Training linear probes on residual stream activations at the last token before CoT, we can predict the model's final answer with 0.9 AUC on most tasks. We find that these directions are not only predictive, but also causal: steering activations along the probe direction flips model answers in over 50% of cases, significantly exceeding orthogonal baselines. When steering induces incorrect answers, we observe two distinct failure modes: non-entailment (stating correct premises but drawing unsupported conclusions) and confabulation (fabricating false premises). While post-hoc reasoning may be instrumentally useful when the model has a correct pre-CoT belief, these failure modes suggest it can result in undesirable behaviors when reasoning from a false belief."

## Key Findings

**Linear Probe Results:**
- Researchers achieved "0.9 AUC on most tasks" when predicting final answers from pre-CoT activations
- These predictive directions proved causally influential

**Activation Steering:**
- Manipulating activations "flips model answers in over 50% of cases"
- Performance significantly surpassed orthogonal control baselines

**Models and Tasks:**
The paper does not specify particular model architectures or task names in the abstract provided.

## Implications for CoT Faithfulness

The research challenges the assumption that chain-of-thought reasoning faithfully represents decision-making. Models appear to decide answers first, then generate post-hoc explanations—raising concerns about whether verbalized reasoning genuinely reflects underlying processes or merely rationalizes predetermined conclusions.

PC-LDCD uses a sigmoid-gated system: "βt = σ(𝒮NLL(zt) − τ)" where τ is calibrated from validation data by maximizing F1 score on a precision-recall curve. When βt < 0.05, the system bypasses intervention entirely, defaulting to standard decoding. When anomalies are detected (higher βt values), the method performs k-candidate lookahead in token space, selecting tokens that maximize: "log PLM(ci|x<t) − βt · 𝒮NLL(fϕ(ht+1(ci)))"

## 2) Computational Overhead

Per-token costs include three components:
- MLP projection: O(DLLM · DPC)
- Circuit evaluation: O(|N|) where |N| ≈ 1000 nodes
- Lookahead (anomalous tokens only): IGR · k · dblock

The paper reports "PC scoring cost is below 2% of one full transformer-layer forward pass," with lookahead dominating at approximately 41-78% intervention rate across models tested.

## 3) Training Process

PCNet and projection bottleneck are jointly trained using a composite loss: "α·E[−log𝒞root(z+)] + (1−α)·E[max(0, γ + log𝒞root(z−) − log𝒞root(z+))]"

Default configuration uses 500 balanced samples (250 factual/250 hallucinated), 50 epochs, 8-sample batch size, 10⁻³ learning rate, with gradient clipping at ‖∇‖₂ ≤ 1.0.

## 4) Circuit Architecture

The probabilistic circuit features:
- Depth: 4 layers with branching factor 3
- Input nodes: heterogeneous leaf mixtures of Gaussian, Laplace, and Student-T distributions
- Projection: 128-dimensional MLP bottleneck compressing from 4096-dimensional LLM hidden states
- Total nodes: approximately 1000

## 5) Operational Granularity

PC-LDCD operates at token-level granularity per decoding step, evaluating "the final-layer hidden state corresponding strictly to the last valid token" at each generation step.

**Probe Architecture**: Lightweight linear probe on dimensionality-reduced residual stream activations to predict whether a generated reasoning step faithfully reflects the model's internal computation. Architecture: f(h) = σ(wT(Wproj · hresidual) + b) where Wproj ∈ R^(d_proj × d_model) is the learned projection (d_proj ∈ {1, 16, 64, 128}). The choice of residual stream over attention heads is motivated by: (a) Decoding Answers Before CoT shows residual stream linearly encodes the model's pre-determined answer (0.9 AUC); (b) Single Direction of Truth shows faithfulness signals are linearly encoded in residual stream; (c) the Mapping Gap finding that residual stream encodes information not expressed in output—this divergence IS the faithfulness signal.

**Engaging with the Mapping Gap**: We argue the Mapping Gap SUPPORTS faithfulness detection: (a) The gap IS our signal—when internal representations systematically diverge from output text, the residual stream at the final token of a step encodes both what the model computed and what it outputs. (b) Decoding Answers Before CoT provides direct evidence: probes detect pre-determined answers that the model may subsequently rationalize unfaithfully. (c) We need to DETECT the gap (flag divergence), not BRIDGE it (force faithful output). (d) The pilot resolves this empirically.

**Training Data Pipeline**: (1) Primary: FaithCoT-Bench's ~1500 step-level labels from expert annotations across 4 domains, generated by running Qwen3.6-27B on FaithCoT-Bench problems and mapping expert faithfulness judgments to model-specific activations. (2) Secondary expansion: FUR unlearning protocol for ~3000 additional synthetic labels. (3) Data efficiency mitigations: (a) 128-dim bottleneck reduces effective dimensionality by 28× (3584→128), making 1500 samples well above the ~10:1 sample-to-parameter ratio needed for logistic regression on 128 features; (b) L2 regularization with strength selected via cross-validation prevents overfitting; (c) PC-LDCD demonstrates that 500 balanced samples suffice for residual-stream-based detection with similar dimensionality reduction; (d) if the faithfulness signal is truly 1-dimensional (per Single Direction of Truth), 1500 samples is >1000× the minimum needed. (4) Evaluation: Leave-one-domain-out cross-validation (4 folds) for generalization; 20% within-domain holdout for calibration.

**Step Boundary Detection**: Double-newline delimiters within <think> blocks for reasoning models. Minimum 20-token threshold. **Reasoning Horizon optimization**: Concentrate monitoring on steps within first 70-85% of chain length where faithfulness violations are most consequential (arXiv 2602.11201). Ablation: full-chain vs. horizon-aware monitoring.

**Inference-Time Rejection Loop**: After generating each step: (1) Extract residual stream at final token. (2) Project and evaluate: p_faithful = f(Wproj · hresidual). (3) If p_faithful > τ: accept. (4) If p_faithful ≤ τ: reject and invoke diversity mechanism. (5) Maximum 3 rejection attempts; graceful degradation to highest-scoring attempt.

**Contribution 2: Computational Diversity Verification (Novel Technical Contribution)**

Hidden Error Awareness documents that 'the model generates its correction using the same flawed computation that produced the original error.' This is the fundamental challenge for ANY rejection-based approach: surface diversity (different words) may mask computational uniformity (same unfaithful reasoning expressed differently). We introduce computational diversity verification as a direct, measurable test of whether regeneration produces genuinely different computation:

**(a) Surface diversity** (baseline): 4-gram suppression of rejected step + temperature scaling (T=1.2→1.5 on successive rejections). Forces different token sequences as minimum diversity.

**(b) Computational diversity verification** (headline contribution): After regeneration, compare projected residual stream activations: sim(Wproj · hregen, Wproj · horig). If cosine similarity > δ (e.g., 0.92), the regeneration produced the same computation in different words—the intervention FAILED to create computational diversity. This transforms the 'same computation' problem from an untestable philosophical concern into a measurable empirical signal. We report: (i) what fraction of regenerations pass surface diversity but fail computational diversity (quantifying the gap between textual and computational diversity); (ii) whether computational diversity correlates with faithfulness improvement (validating that different computation → more faithful output); (iii) how δ threshold affects the diversity-quality tradeoff.

**(c) Conditioning perturbation** (escalation when diversity verification fails): Rephrase the previous accepted step via lightweight paraphrase, then regenerate current step from modified prefix. This changes the INPUT to computation, forcing genuinely different processing.

This three-level mechanism is independently valuable as a diagnostic tool: even if SFGRD's faithfulness probes underperform, the computational diversity verification framework provides the first quantitative measurement of whether rejection sampling creates genuinely different reasoning or merely surface variation—directly testing Hidden Error Awareness's 'same computation' thesis with measurable evidence.

**Safety Motivation (Why Faithfulness Matters for Correct Answers)**:

The question 'why enforce faithfulness on correct answers?' has a precise safety answer:

(1) **CoT monitoring reliability**: Chain of Thought Monitorability (arXiv 2507.11473) establishes CoT monitoring as a fragile but critical safety mechanism. If 15-20% of correct outputs use reasoning that doesn't reflect actual computation, monitors cannot reliably detect intent to misbehave—documented cases show models producing benign-seeming reasoning while implementing harmful actions.

(2) **Distribution shift fragility**: A model that arrives at a correct answer via internal computation X but reports reasoning Y will fail when the problem shifts to require Y-like reasoning that the model doesn't actually perform. Unfaithful-but-correct is a leading indicator of fragile correctness.

(3) **Deceptive alignment precondition**: Systematic divergence between stated reasoning and internal computation is precisely the capability needed for deceptive alignment. Reducing this divergence at inference time is a direct safety intervention.

**Positioning Within the Paradigm**: SFGRD does NOT claim architectural novelty—the detect-and-intervene-during-generation pattern is established by DHC, Token-Guard, PC-LDCD, and Monitoring Decoding. SFGRD's contributions are: (a) bringing this proven paradigm to the UNADDRESSED target of faithfulness (text vs. internal computation), completing the correctness-factuality-faithfulness trilogy; (b) computational diversity verification as a novel mechanism that addresses the fundamental 'same computation' challenge unique to faithfulness intervention (factuality methods can regenerate from external knowledge; faithfulness methods must ensure the model actually computes differently).

(b) Step-level vs. token-level granularity. (c) Supervised probes with faithfulness labels vs. unsupervised density estimation. (d) Includes computational diversity verification (PC-LDCD's contrastive decoding does not verify whether intervention changed the underlying computation). (e) Shared strategy: dimensionality reduction bottleneck for data-efficient training.

**Key Differentiators from DHC**: (a) Targets faithfulness, not correctness. (b) Residual stream probes (full computational state) vs. attention head probes (local patterns). (c) Rejection sampling with diversity verification vs. beam search. (d) Addresses 'same computation' problem that beam search does not consider.

**Key Differentiators from Token-Guard**: (a) Faithfulness vs. factuality. (b) Step vs. token granularity. (c) Trained probes vs. unsupervised cosine similarity. (d) Computational diversity verification vs. simple regeneration.

**Baselines**: (1) Greedy decoding. (2) DHC beam search with correctness probes (reproduction). (3) DHC beam search with faithfulness probes (direct comparison—same probe, different decoding). (4) Self-consistency (majority voting). (5) Probe-guided best-of-N (replicating Hidden Error Awareness's failure). (6) Token-Guard-style latent-space scoring adapted to step level. (7) PC-LDCD-style density estimation adapted to step level (ablation isolating supervised vs. unsupervised detection for faithfulness).

**Evaluation**: Primary model: Qwen3.6-27B. Datasets: GSM8K (mathematical) + GPQA (knowledge-intensive). Metrics: (a) Faithfulness improvement via FaithCoT-Bench protocol. (b) Accuracy preservation (≤1% degradation acceptable). (c) Latency overhead (target: <2x greedy). (d) Rejection rate.
